content: Aspire's ServiceDefaults template gates /health and /alive behind IsDevelopment() by default specifically because unauthenticated health endpoints have security implications if exposed publicly (info disclosure, minor DoS surface). Microsoft's official guidance for exposing them outside Development is to add caching, timeouts, and authorization/host-filtering — not to leave them ungated. This phase's D-11 substitutes network-topology isolation (Tailnet-only, port never published) for that app-level protection, which is an accepted, explicitly reasoned deviation from the template default, not an oversight.
